initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The patient, a 69-year-old Chinese male, was admitted for the primary complaint of intermittent gross hematuria that had been present for 10 days. Before admission, the patient underwent a B ultrasound in our department, which revealed hypoechoic nodules in the right upper wall of the bladder (cystoscopy was recommended), prostate enlargement with calcification, and no abnormal findings in either kidney. No distention of the ureters was observed, and about 91 ml of residual bladder urine was present. There are no special past interventions. The physical examination did not reveal any positive findings.

evidence_items.source_text: Before admission, the patient underwent a B ultrasound in our department, which revealed hypoechoic nodules in the right upper wall of the bladder (cystoscopy was recommended), prostate enlargement with calcification, and no abnormal findings in either kidney. No distention of the ureters was observed, and about 91 ml of residual bladder urine was present (Fig. 1).
Cystoscopy revealed a 3.0 × 3.0 cm globular mass in the right anterior wall of the bladder, with a narrow pedicle, and the formation of sheet-like yellow calcification on the surface of the mass

In July 2023, a transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBt) with cystoscopic multipoint random biopsy was performed. The postoperative pathological examination results showed the presence of pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma in the adult bladder (Fig. 3). A tumor biopsy taken at the time of TURBt showed no residual tumor in the bladder muscularis.
A pre-chemotherapy positron emission tomography–computed tomography (PET-CT) scan did not reveal any metastatic lesions throughout the body.

In addition, we also performed a next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the tumor tissue to detect the presence of chromosomal abnormalities or gene mutations. The result of gene analysis was the gene variation of TP53 (exon 7 c.743G > T p,(R248L) NM_000546.5) with a mutation abundance of 91.77% and MAPK1 amplification with a copy number of 5.78. And the microsatellite stability status is microsatellite stable (MSS).

To exclude the possibility of neuroendocrine carcinoma, undifferentiated carcinoma, sarcomatoid carcinoma, or high-grade lymphoma, we performed an immunohistochemical analysis of this sample. The immunohistochemical results were GATA3 (epithelial +), P53 (tumor: 90%+), KI67 (tumor: 45%+), CK (−), KI67 (45%+), GATA3 (−), SMA (−), vimentin (+), MyoD 1 ( +; Fig. 4), myogenin (partial +; Fig.

The chemotherapy regimen administered was intravenous dacarbazine with doxorubicin. The chemotherapy regimen administered was intravenous. With the treatment of dacarbazine with doxorubicin, the patient had good adherence and tolerability There was no adverse event due to chemotherapy.
